summary:
In orbital freefall (0G), natural buoyancy vanishes (Gr -> 0, Ra -> 0). Hot gases do not rise, smoke does not collect at the ceiling, liquid droplets burn as symmetric blue spheres that transition into invisible 550–750 K cool flames, and gentle cabin ventilation (3–8 cm/s) allows solid polymers to burn below Earth's minimum oxygen concentration (MOC). Meanwhile, decades of NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) combustion records remain scattered across heterogeneous tables and reports.

ALTAR-NASA (v6.3) is an open-source (Apache-2.0), zero-install engineering workbench and 3D digital twin built for the Flame in Freefall challenge. Across five integrated modules, it couples closed-form transport laws (Godsave–Spalding d-squared, de Ris solid flame spread, Burke–Schumann gas diffusion, and 21-point MOC +/-1 sigma maps) with 36+ NASA PSI investigations (FLEX, CFI, BASS, Saffire I–VI, SoFIE, ACME, SAME/DAFT), live NASA OSDR/NTRS telemetry queries, RGB/HSV flame computer vision, a safe AST equation verifier, offline misconception-guarded engineering analysis, and an interactive 5-compartment 3D Orion MCP spacecraft executing a 5-step non-Halon fine water-mist fire response. The platform runs instantly in any web browser or offline on Windows, protecting Artemis crews while advancing terrestrial cleanroom and EV battery fire safety.
details:
Live Browser App (Zero Install): https://faruk042.github.io/NASA-ENGLISH/

Open Source Repository (Apache 2.0): https://github.com/Faruk042/NASA-ENGLISH

Standalone Windows Desktop App (Nasa_4.exe): https://github.com/Faruk042/NASA-ENGLISH/releases/latest

1. Complete Platform Scope Across Five Integrated Modules

ALTAR-NASA connects NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) and Technical Reports Server (NTRS) microgravity combustion records directly to spacecraft fire prevention, detection, and suppression engineering across five integrated workspaces.

3D WebGL Combustion Chamber, Coupled Physics and Material Certification (Tab 1):

The physics engine solves closed-form Godsave and Spalding d-squared droplet regression, de Ris opposed and concurrent solid flame spread, Burke and Schumann gas burner diffusion, Ranz and Marshall Sherwood transport, Damkohler residence numbers, and radiative heat-loss quenching. It models 550 to 750 K negative-temperature-coefficient invisible cool flames alongside real-time Web Audio flame sonification. Predictions are continuously benchmarked (R-squared and RMSE) against International Space Station FLEX, CFI, and BASS flight data. Users can plot 21-point minimum oxygen concentration (MOC) flammability maps with one-sigma uncertainty bands across 0G, Lunar (0.16G), Martian (0.38G), and Earth (1G) gravity levels, test custom cabin polymers (PEEK, PTFE, Kapton, XLPE, Nomex, PMMA) via thermal inertia analog matching, verify compliance across five mission atmospheres under NASA-STD-6001B, and monitor crew survival margins against NASA JSC-20584 carbon monoxide SMAC limits (25, 100, and 425 ppm).

5-Compartment 3D Orion MCP Spacecraft and 5-Step Fire Response (Tab 1 Spacecraft Mode):

An interactive 3D digital twin models the Command, Living, Power and Avionics, Docking Tunnel, and Airlock compartments in Exterior and Cutaway X-Ray views with Optical, long-wave infrared thermal (LWIR Ironbow), Split-View, and live Webcam flame-flicker camera feeds. During a fire test, the spacecraft executes a hardware-interlocked five-step response: (1) multi-channel optical, thermal, and carbon monoxide confirmation, (2) inter-module ventilation fan shutoff to stop oxygen supply, (3) 120 VDC power bus isolation and hatch sealing, (4) sub-40-micron SoFIE-MIST fine water-mist suppression (Halon 1301 is strictly blocked per NASA-STD-6001B because flame pyrolysis produces toxic HF and HBr acid gases), and (5) 0G hot-core cooling below 525 K followed by CAMRAS cabin air scrubbing to prevent flash re-ignition.

Dynamic NASA PSI Ranking, Intra-Run Variations and Earth Spinoffs (Tab 2):

The platform ranks 15 detailed NASA flight campaigns and a 36-study PSI archive by combining Euclidean thermodynamic proximity (32 percent), mission hazard weight (24 percent), and TF-IDF semantic relevance (44 percent). Engineers can compare multi-run parameter matrices side by side and explore terrestrial safety applications, including SAME and DAFT dual-wavelength dust-immune smoke detectors for mines and aircraft cargo bays, and SoFIE-MIST low-water suppression for cleanrooms and electric vehicle lithium-ion battery facilities.

Live NASA OSDR and NTRS Stream, Computer Vision and Safe AST Verifier (Tab 3):

Users can query official psi.nasa.gov, osdr.nasa.gov, and ntrs.nasa.gov APIs in real time with automatic offline archive fallback, parse multi-file dataset bundles (CSV, TSV, XLSX, ZIP, JSON, and PDF) with automatic unit normalization, segment flame photographs and videos in RGB and HSV color spaces to measure 0G sphericity, blue chemiluminescence, yellow soot radiance, and flame standoff ratios, and test custom correlations safely through a whitelist Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parser without code execution risks.

Misconception-Guarded Engineering Analysis and Offline Architecture (Tabs 4 and 5):

Decision-support reports run completely offline through the deterministic analytical solver or a local Ollama language model on 127.0.0.1. A domain scope and physics verifier catches common microgravity misconceptions, such as placing smoke sensors on a 0G ceiling, pouring bulk liquid water in freefall, or opening a sealed hatch before hot-core cooling completes, displaying a clear Physics Note explanation. Scenarios apply directly to the 3D scene in one click, export as standalone HTML or PDF engineering reports, and run under strict loopback, CSRF, and Content Security Policy isolation.

2. Super Intelligence (SI) and Tooling Disclosure

All numerical telemetry (flame temperature, burn rate constant, transfer numbers, Sherwood and Damkohler ratios, MOC curves, and SMAC survival times) is computed strictly by deterministic physical equations with zero generative math hallucination. In-app analytics rely on classical TF-IDF retrieval, deterministic RGB and HSV computer vision, and optional local or cloud language models for natural-language questions. During development, AI coding and writing tools (Google Gemini and Antigravity IDE) assisted with UI scaffolding, English localization, automated self-tests, and documentation editing, while neural text-to-speech (TTS) generated the English voiceover narration for our real-software demo video.
